newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ok Tedi mine still hit by drought - BHP.
newsitem.headline: Ok Tedi mine still hit by drought - BHP.

text.p: The Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea remains paralysed by drought, a spokesman for the operator, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday.
"We're really just focusing on removing waste and exposing ore at this stage," the spokesman said.
A stockpile of some 150,000 tonnes of concentrates on hand would be shipped down the Fly River via barges once the drought had passed, he said.
The mine, located in PNG's western province, was forced last Sunday to shut the second of two semi-autogenous grinding mills after reviewing supplies of diesel fuel.
The mine's other mill was shut a week earlier as a result of the dry weather spell affecting the country's highlands region.
BHP was keeping in contact with customers around the world, who have agreed to adjust their shipping schedules during the drought, the spokesman said.
A declaration of force majeure -- circumstances beyond the control of the mine preventing it from meeting its supply contract -- was not currently being considered, the spokesman said.
"We have been talking to the smelters and they have been very cooperative given the circumstances," the spokesman said.
